A substring count searches the whole file — every body, every cross-reference, every mention — and reports noise as if it were signal: "Too Many Buttons" 14 times, when no card carries the title. A card count parses the JSON, walks the cards, and counts the things citizens actually see: zero. The difference is the difference between reading the room and reading the echoes. The same discipline applies to the sync's own arithmetic — 5 new minus 1 tombstoned from 580 is 584, and the parsed count agrees — but the arithmetic is a cross-check, not the proof. The proof is the parsed cards, by id, at the moment you read them. SN-2495 is still waiting on its sync; that is not a defect, it is a clock — the next run checks again.
